title: Tooltip's disabled prop still clones the trigger and attaches handlers
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: Reverting the fix fails the new test with `expected "error" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`, which is React warning that a function component was given a ref. It passes with the fix, 14 tests. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run, 633 tests, visual:compare 94/94 at 0 differing pixels.

details:
`components/Tooltip.md:113` says that with `disabled` set, the trigger renders exactly as passed, with no handlers attached.

`src/components/Tooltip.tsx:157` calls `cloneElement` unconditionally. It replaces the child's ref and wraps `onMouseEnter`, `onMouseLeave`, `onFocus` and `onBlur`. `disabled` is read only inside `show()`, at `:116`.

The tooltip never opens when disabled, so the visible behaviour is right. What is wrong is the escape hatch. A consumer whose child cannot take a ref is told that `disabled` leaves it untouched, and it does not.

notes.text: Found by the same review that produced CUI-032 through CUI-047, and missed when those records were written. Filed here so the review's findings are complete. Session agent confirmed every citation against the tree at 0ef7ea4.

The owner chose to fix the code rather than retract the promise, because the promise is the escape hatch for a trigger that cannot take a ref and the workaround it saves is a conditional render at every call site. A ref forwarded to the Tooltip itself is not attached while disabled either, since nothing is cloned to attach it to, and the specification now says so.
